content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Combining Error Handling and Business Logic focuses on the following parts of the supplied syllabus: Handling missing lookup results; Distinguishing genuine zero values from missing data; Avoiding formulas that conceal important errors. Keep the underlying source data visible and make each assumption explicit.

content_blocks.expected_output: Returns the matching value from the lookup table, or a not-found result for the XLOOKUP example. Use the exact/appropriate match mode for the chosen method.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Check that lookup and return ranges align, IDs use the same data type, and keys are unique where required. XLOOKUP is not available in every older Excel version; VLOOKUP and INDEX/MATCH remain useful for compatibility.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Work in a duplicate workbook or a scratch sheet. Restore the input range and formula/code to the original state, clear filters or selections, then rerun the same test cases. Record expected and actual behavior rather than assuming a successful result.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with a small, known dataset for combining error handling and business logic. Apply the example above, compute or inspect at least one result independently, then deliberately try a blank, duplicate, boundary, or not-found case where relevant.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small worksheet or workbook section that demonstrates combining error handling and business logic. Use clear headers, label units and assumptions, and capture expected versus actual output for a normal case and an edge case. Where the concept requires a specialized Excel feature, first verify that feature is available in your Excel edition.
